My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

Steps.Message:
What will happen next?

We have been alerted to a potentially dangerous situation involving a tree causing a low hanging overhead line, so have responded as quickly as possible and asked our control room to turn power off to the area using our high voltage network. This is why a wide area has lost electricity.

Once further specialist field staff have assessed the situation, we'll start diverting power back to affected homes as soon as they advise us it's safe. You may notice your lights going on and off as we work to get as much power restored as we can.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing, but we'll always try to give you the clearest information we have.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Sent by Donny at 13:02 - We're very sorry we've had to switch off your electricity. Our engineers have turned off the power in the Pulborough RH20 4 area in the interest of the public's health and safety. This is so they can investigate reports of a low overhead line caused by a fallen tree.

If in the area, please take care and stay at least 10m away from the cable. 

Until our engineers arrive on site and investigate, it's difficult to advise you a time frame. However, based on an average for this kind of issue, our estimated time to have you back on is between 19:00-20:00. 

We'll keep you updated with our progress, but in the meantime our team are always here to talk on 105 if you have any questions or concerns.

Sent by Kevin at 16:05 - Just another check in from us, as we know power being off for longer periods can be very disruptive, and we just wanted to help explain why it can take longer to get power restored safely during bad weather like we're having at the moment.

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

Logs.Comment:
Sent by Kevin at 16:27 - We believe our engineers have been able to restore power to all 219 customers in the Lewes BN8 5 area by diverting power around an overhead network fault.  We're pleased that we have been able to restore power sooner than we estimated.

If your power isn't back on, we'll need to hear from you. To report this, or to talk to us about anything else, call us on 08003163105 which is free from landlines and mobiles.

We know that being without power can be worrying, but please rest assured that our staff work around the clock to keep the lights on. If you have any concerns or questions, give us a call any time.

What will happen next?

This outage is affecting multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you'd expect. We have already sent staff to the area, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting the electricity around the faulty section. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to restore as much power as we can.

The engineer will head to the local substation and after checking the network, will attempt to restore more power from there. If unsuccessful, they will locate and repair the issue, which will take longer to get the lights on.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing, but we'll always try to give you the clearest information we have.

Sent by Kevin at 15:53 - Our engineers are on their way. We believe the issue is on our overhead network that initially interrupted power to 219 properties.

However, we have managed to divert power back to some properties, so 51 properties are still affected. Specialist engineers from our control room will continue to divert power remotely, so your power may come back on at any point. Sometimes we can't restore everyone this way, so we're also sending staff to check our equipment.

We're currently estimating power will be on between 22:00 and 23:00, but this may change depending on what our staff find.

Power back on? To stop receiving texts, follow this link https://UKPN.short.gy/STOP to unsubscribe. Otherwise, we'll keep you updated.

Sent by Decasta at 19:45 - I wanted to reach out to say that our staff are doing everything they can to get your lights back on. Heavy rain and strong winds like we're experiencing with Storm Austen and Storm Boelo can make things harder for our engineers, especially when trying to repair overhead cabling.

While the weather is impacting our network, damage to our cabling can still occur. Usually, this is due to trees being swayed by the wind and making contact with a cable or piece of pole mounted network equipment, like a transformer.

When this happens, it can create potentially dangerous situations, so if you spot anything wrong with our equipment or cabling, please stay away from the area and call our team on 105, pressing the option for emergencies.

Logs.Comment:
Sent by Decasta at 19:49 - I wanted to reach out to say that our staff are doing everything they can to get your lights back on. Heavy rain and strong winds like we're experiencing with Storm Austen and Storm Boelo can make things harder for our engineers, especially when trying to repair overhead cabling.

While the weather is impacting our network, damage to our cabling can still occur. Usually, this is due to trees being swayed by the wind making contact with a cable or piece of pole mounted network equipment, like a transformer.

When this happens, it can create potentially dangerous situations. If you spot anything wrong with our equipment or cabling, please stay away from the area and call our team on 105, pressing the option for emergencies.

Sent by Decasta at 18:15 -

We're sorry for the disruption to your power today, especially for those who may be more vulnerable without the electric. If you're worried about an elderly or ill person in your property who is affected by the power cut today, we are able to provide some support. For more information just click here: https://UKPN.short.gy/PSR
 
If you have any further concerns or questions though, don't hesitate to call us free on 08003163105. We'll continue to keep you updated with our engineer's progress.

Our engineers have arrived on site in the Canterbury CT2 area and are investigating the fault.

You may find your power is going on and off; that is normal for this type of issue and is due to our engineers working to divert power remotely. By doing this, we've managed to restore power to 488 customers. There are now 351 properties still affected and using an average time frame we're estimating all power will be on between 23:00 and 00:00, but this may change later depending on what our staff find.

We'll keep sending SMS updates until everybody is restored. To stop receiving texts, just follow this link https://UKPN.short.gy/STOP to unsubscribe. Sent by Kevin at 17:22.

Thanks for your patience today. We know a power cut can be difficult, especially in colder weather.

Many properties have gas hobs, which can still be used in a power cut for cooking, or heating water for drinks and sterilisation of baby bottles. The spark to ignite the hob will not work however, so if you do use it please take extra care when using other ignition sources like matches or lighters. Even in daytime, the light in your house may be low in a power cut, so only do this if you are confident it can be done safely.

If you have any questions or concerns, our team are always on hand to help.

Logs.Comment:
Sent by Bradley  at 21:24 - We can now confirm that all power in the Fulham Road area should be back on. The issue was caused by an unexpected fault with some of our network equipment, which our engineers have now replaced.

We know that being without power can be especially difficult, so we're sorry for the outage. Please rest assured our staff will continue to work around the clock to keep the lights on.

If your power isn't on or there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us on 08003163105 which is free from landlines and mobiles.

Our engineers have now arrived on site in the Fulham Road area.

As any issues that currently exist on our network have affected our equipment at the substation, engineers will start their testing there. They will then check our network equipment throughout the area to try and identify any problems, before trying to restore power.

Our estimated time frame of 23:30 and 00:30 hasn't changed, but if this is not successful it's possible that a cable repair may be needed. This can involve ground excavations, traffic management equipment or specialist teams. As soon as our staff can safely update us, we'll give you the latest news. Sent by Bradley  at 20:26.

Steps.Message:
We're sorry if your power is still off. Due to the high winds and heavy rain from Storm Austen impacting our network, we're dealing with more power cuts than usual.
 
Our staff are working 24/7 to help customers and fix these problems, though due to extra reports of damage and the difficult conditions, it's taking us longer to get everything repaired and the lights back on.
 
We think it's unlikely we will be able to restore your electricity tonight. We are now estimating we'll restore your power between 11:00 and 12:00. This is not the message we want to send, but we want to provide you with realistic updates so you can plan ahead.
 
Sent by Milly at 22:04.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message: Our engineers have arrived on site in the Cranbrook TN17 area and are investigating the overhead network fault. You may find your power is going on and off; that is normal for this type of issue and is due to our engineers working to divert power remotely. By doing this, we've managed to restore power to 2991 customers. There are now 109 properties still affected and using an average time frame we're estimating all power will be on between 00:00-01:00, but this may change later depending on what our staff find. We'll keep sending SMS updates until everybody is restored. To stop receiving texts, just follow this link https://UKPN.short.gy/STOP to unsubscribe. Sent by Decasta at 19:42.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
What will happen next?

This outage is affecting multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you'd expect. We have already sent staff to the area, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting the electricity around the faulty section. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to restore as much power as we can.

The engineer will head to the local substation and after checking the network, will attempt to restore more power from there. If unsuccessful, they will locate and repair the issue, which will take longer to get the lights on.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing, but we'll always try to give you the clearest information we have.

based on an average for this kind of issue, our estimated time to have you back on is between 20:00 and 21:00.

Steps.Message:
Sent by Jack at 23:53 - Just another check in from us, as we know power being off for longer periods can be very disruptive, and we just wanted to help explain why it can take longer to get power restored safely during bad weather like we're having at the moment.

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Sent by Theo at 00:22 - Just another check in from us, as we know power being off for longer periods can be very disruptive, and we just wanted to help explain why it can take longer to get power restored safely during bad weather like we're having at the moment.

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

Our staff are working 24/7 to help customers and fix these problems, though due to extra reports of damage and the difficult conditions, it's taking us longer to get everything repaired and the lights back on.
 
We think it's unlikely we will be able to restore your electricity tonight. We are now estimating we'll restore your power between 11:30 and 12:30. This is not the message we want to send, but we want to provide you with realistic updates so you can plan ahead.
 
Sent by Milly at 23:50.

PlannedIncidentReason: We're carrying out planned work in your area. For our engineers to carry it out safely they need to turn the power off. We're doing this work as it's essential to provide reliable electricity supplies to your area. We're sorry for any inconvenience caused and thank you for your patience.
MainMessage: We are currently experiencing problems with the electricity supply in your area.  Our engineers have attended the fault, and have made an emergency repair to restore power to as many premises as possible.  It is our intention to return to make a permanent repair as soon as we can.  I'm sorry, but we can't give you a time for this at present. Please accept our sincere apologies for any inconvenience this may cause.

Every outage is fully investigated by our engineers, though power may be lost several times before we can safely find and fix the issue. Our customer services team will keep as many customers updated as possible during these investigations.

To talk to us, or let us know that your power isn't restored, call us on 08003163105.

It is our intention to return to make a permanent repair as soon as we can.  I'm sorry, but we can't give you a time for this at present. Please accept our sincere apologies for any inconvenience this may cause.

Steps.Message:
Sent by Theo at 00:05 - Our engineers are on their way. At this point we think the issue is an overhead network fault affecting 178 properties.

Specialist engineers from our control room are also working to divert power remotely, so it's possible your power could come back on at any point. We can't always restore everyone this way. That's why we're also sending staff to the area to check our equipment.

Every fault is different, so our time frames have to be estimated but currently we hope to have power back on between 04:30 and 05:30. We must stress that it may become necessary for this to change, depending on what our engineers find.

We'll keep you updated with our progress.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message: We became aware of this power cut at 22:50. We’re sorry for any disruption this may have caused you. We didn’t know in advance there would be a power cut, but now that we know, our teams will do everything they can to get your power back quickly. Engineers in our control room have switched some customers power back on in your area. To get everyone’s power back on we may need to attend to investigate and make repairs. We’ll continue to update you until everyone’s power is back on.

Steps.Message: We have engineers on their way. As this is affecting your area, they will not need to attend your property. Rest assured once they arrive, they’ll work as quickly as is safely possible to get your power back on.

Steps.Message:
What will happen next?

This outage affects multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you expect. We're arranging staff to attend ASAP, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting electricity. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to get as many customers back on as we can.

Once available, our engineer will head to the local substation and after checking the network, they will attempt to restore more power from there. If unsuccessful, they will work to locate the issue and make repairs, which may take longer to get the lights on.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing but we'll always give you the clearest information we have.

PlannedIncidentReason: We're carrying out planned work in your area. For our engineers to carry it out safely they need to turn the power off. We're doing this work as it's essential to provide reliable electricity supplies to your area. We're sorry for any inconvenience caused and thank you for your patience.
MainMessage: We are currently experiencing problems with the electricity supply in your area.  We are arranging to have engineers investigate the fault.  We are sorry we can't give you a time for the restoration of supply at present. Please accept our sincere apologies for any inconvenience this may cause.
